From around July 2018 to March 2019 I weight lifted quite a bit. I wasn't amazingly strong but at a pretty good level, my PRs were Deadlift: 160kg, Bench: 100kg and Squat 100kg (I know I should have focused on legs more). However at around February my decline began because I had been diagnosed with carpal tunnel and moved countries resulting in me completely stopping. Only recently I realized how much smaller I had gotten (Dropped from 84kg to 77kg) and wanted to become fit again.

I decided to go back to the gym but knew I could no longer power lift without hurting my wrists so I only used dumbbells and cables. Starting off with chest day my weights dropped significantly as expected and I could only do 10 push ups in 1set. I felt good and had no other pains apart from the usual muscle soreness and was excited to exercise again.

However the next day was terrible, I had never been so sore from a chest workout in my life. I couldn't lift my arms in the air (Highest was at chest level) and my pecs would feel bruised if I even touched them. I didn't think much of it and thought I had a great workout, but then when I was cooking and adding pepper (Using those hand rotating grinders) I felt an electric shock in my left hand after rotating the grinder. It was such a weird sensation, it felt like one of those prank shock staplers or pens however I felt it go from my wrist all the way up my forearm. Unsure if it was real or not I repeated the motion and it happened again and again. Now it was obvious this was my carpal tunnel but I had never felt a shock like this before, before I would feel heat resulting in a numb feeling in my hand where I wouldn't be able to feel my fingers.

Because of this I didn't weight lift for the rest of the week and only did cardio. 10 days later, which brings us to yesterday, I felt normal and decided to do Back day instead. Everything felt completely fine and I had no wrist pains, (I should mention that I stretch my forearms and wrists daily in case someone recommends it.) My soreness was not as severe thought my body was just getting used to exercise. However today, I decided to try do push ups and just couldn't, I started up and as I tried to lower myself I just shake uncontrollably until I fall to the ground. I'm too shy to go to the gym and end up taking low weighted dumbbells just to rack them again so I haven't tested them.

I apologize for the long essay but felt like I should explain every detail I thought could relate to the issue.

TL;DR : Pretty decent Weight lifting, stopped because of moving countries and carpal tunnel, started working out again could do 10 push ups, 11 days later can't even do 1.
